coverageNotes: Tests identical-call OCC/idempotency outcome only. Whole-mutation rollback is shared with 004-cascade_delete/q004-2. Full validation, mismatched key reuse, and atomic cache implementation remain unconverted.

questions.question: What do the clients receive, and what is committed?

options.text: Both calls succeed with different transfer IDs. Two records are inserted, and the balances become 80 and 120.
options.rationale: The lookup and writes run in one mutation. Conflicting attempts retry; observed calls commit one transfer rather than two.

options.text: Both calls succeed with the same transfer ID. One record is inserted, and the balances become 90 and 110.
options.rationale: Both calls return the same committed record and balances move once. A conflicting attempt can retry and observe that record.

options.text: One call succeeds and one fails because the index rejects a duplicate key. One record is inserted, and the balances become 90 and 110.
options.rationale: An ordinary index does not reject duplicate-key inserts. A targeted control inserts duplicates successfully and unique() rejects a later read.

options.text: One call succeeds and one fails because Convex reports the write conflict to that client. One record is inserted, and the balances become 90 and 110.
options.rationale: The initial conflict is retried automatically. Runtime retry logs accompany fulfilled calls; this does not promise unlimited retries under arbitrary contention.
